## 1. Section on Roots (Mūlavāra)

## 1. Wholesome States (1) Root Method (Mūlanaya)

(a) Whatever states are wholesome, are all those wholesome roots? There are only three wholesome roots (non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion). The remaining wholesome states are not wholesome roots.

(b) Or else, whatever states are wholesome roots, are all those wholesome states? Yes (Āmantā).

(a) Whatever states are wholesome, do all those have the same root as the wholesome root? Yes.

(b) Or else, whatever states have the same root as the wholesome root, are all those...
7:
...wholesome states?

Matter originated by wholesome [consciousness] (kusala-samuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ) has the same root as the wholesome root, but it is not wholesome. A wholesome state both has the same root as the wholesome root and is wholesome.

(a) Whatever states have the same root as the wholesome root, are all those mutually roots by way of the wholesome root?

Those wholesome roots that arise together both have the same root and are mutually roots. The remaining states born along with the wholesome roots have the same root as the wholesome root, but they are not mutually roots.

(b) Or else, whatever states are mutually roots by way of the wholesome root, are all those wholesome states?

Yes.

There are only three root-roots of the wholesome roots. The remaining wholesome states are not root-roots of the wholesome roots.

(b) Or else, whatever states are root-roots of the wholesome roots, are all those wholesome states?

Yes.

(a) Whatever states are wholesome, do all those have the same root-root as the wholesome root?

Yes.

(b) Or else, whatever states have the same root-root as the wholesome root, are all those wholesome states?

(a) Whatever states have the same root-root as the wholesome root, are all those mutually root-roots by way of the wholesome root?

Those wholesome roots that arise together both have the same root-root and are mutually root-roots. The remaining states born along with the wholesome roots have the same root-root as the wholesome root, but they are not mutually root-roots.

(b) Or else, whatever states are mutually root-roots by way of the wholesome root, are all those wholesome states?

Yes.

Yes.

Matter originated by wholesome [consciousness] has wholesome roots, but it is not wholesome. A wholesome state both has wholesome roots and is wholesome.

(a) Whatever states are wholesome, do all those have the same root as the wholesome root?

Yes.

(b) Or else, are all those states that are mutually roots of each other with a wholesome root wholesome? Yes.

For those being reborn in the four-constituent realm and the five-constituent realm, for them in that place both the aggregate of perception will cease and the aggregate of feeling arises.

## (d) Negative Individual (Paccanīkapuggala)
(a) For whom the aggregate of matter does not arise, for that person will the aggregate of feeling not cease?
For all those who are passing away and for those being reborn in the formless realm, for them the aggregate of matter does not arise, but it is not that for them the aggregate of feeling will not cease (it will cease). For those attaining final Nibbāna, for them both the aggregate of matter does not arise and the aggregate of feeling will not cease.

(b) Or else, for whom the aggregate of feeling will not cease, for that person does the aggregate of matter not arise? It is so.

(a) For whom the aggregate of feeling does not arise, for that person will the aggregate of perception not cease?
For all those who are passing away and for those being reborn in the unconscious realm, for them the aggregate of feeling does not arise, but it is not that for them the aggregate of perception will not cease (it will cease).

For those who are attaining Parinibbāna, the aggregate of feeling is not arising, and the aggregate of perception will not cease.

(b) Or else, for whom the aggregate of perception will not cease, for that person is the aggregate of feeling not arising? Yes.

In whatever location the aggregate of matter is not arising... etc.

For those passing away from the five-constituent existence (pañcavokāra) and those in the formless existence (arūpa), in that location the aggregate of matter is not arising, but for them in that location it is not the case that the aggregate of feeling will not cease. For those attaining Parinibbāna and those passing away from the non-percipient existence (asaññasatta), in that location the aggregate of matter is not arising and the aggregate of feeling will not cease.

(b) Or else, for whom in whatever location the aggregate of feeling will not cease, for that person in that location is the aggregate of matter not arising?
For those entering the non-percipient existence, in that location the aggregate of feeling will not cease, but for them in that location it is not the case that the aggregate of matter is not arising. For those attaining Parinibbāna and those passing away from the non-percipient existence, in that location the aggregate of feeling will not cease and the aggregate of matter is not arising.

(a) For whom in whatever location the aggregate of feeling is not arising, for that person in that location will the aggregate of perception not cease?
For those passing away from the four-constituent existence (catuvokāra) and the five-constituent existence, in that location the aggregate of feeling is not arising, but for them in that location it is not the case that the aggregate of perception will not cease. For those attaining Parinibbāna and those in the non-percipient existence, in that location the aggregate of feeling is not arising and the aggregate of perception will not cease.

(b) Or else, for whom in whatever location the aggregate of perception will not cease, for that person in that location is the aggregate of feeling not arising? Yes.

## 3. Section on Full Understanding

## 1. Present Section

(a) He who fully understands the aggregate of matter, does he fully understand the aggregate of feeling? Yes (he does).

(b) Or else, he who fully understands the aggregate of feeling, does he fully understand the aggregate of matter? Yes (he does).

(a) He who does not fully understand the aggregate of matter, does he not fully understand the aggregate of feeling? Yes (he does not).

(b) Or else, he who does not fully understand the aggregate of feeling, does he not fully understand the aggregate of matter? Yes (he does not).

## 2. Past Section

(a) He who has fully understood the aggregate of matter, has he fully understood the aggregate of feeling? Yes (he has).

(b) Or else, he who has fully understood the aggregate of feeling, has he fully understood the aggregate of matter? Yes (he has).

(a) He who has not fully understood the aggregate of matter, has he not fully understood the aggregate of feeling? Yes (he has not).

(b) Or else, he who has not fully understood the aggregate of feeling, has he not fully understood the aggregate of matter? Yes (he has not).

## 3. Future Section

(a) He who will fully understand the aggregate of matter, will he fully understand the aggregate of feeling? Yes (he will).

(b) Or else, he who will fully understand the aggregate of feeling, will he fully understand the aggregate of matter? Yes (he will).
69:
(a) "Will that person who will not fully understand the aggregate of form not fully understand the aggregate of feeling?" Answer: "Yes."
(b) "Or else, will that person who will not fully understand the aggregate of feeling not fully understand the aggregate of form?" Answer: "Yes."

## 4. Paccuppannātītavāro
(a) "Is that person who is fully understanding the aggregate of form one who has fully understood the aggregate of feeling?" Answer: "No."
(b) "Or else, is that person who has fully understood the aggregate of feeling one who is fully understanding the aggregate of form?" Answer: "No."

(a) "Is that person who is not fully understanding the aggregate of form one who has not fully understood the aggregate of feeling?" Answer: "The Arahat is not fully understanding the aggregate of form, but it is not that he has not fully understood the aggregate of feeling. Excluding the one possessed of the path of Arahatship (aggamaggasamaṅgī) and the Arahat, the remaining persons are both not fully understanding the aggregate of form and have not fully understood the aggregate of feeling."
(b) "Or else, is that person who has not fully understood the aggregate of feeling one who is not fully understanding the aggregate of form?" Answer: "The one possessed of the path of Arahatship has not fully understood the aggregate of feeling, but it is not that he is not fully understanding the aggregate of form. Excluding the one possessed of the path of Arahatship and the Arahat, the remaining persons have both not fully understood the aggregate of feeling and are not fully understanding the aggregate of form."

## 5. Paccuppannānāgatavāro
(a) "Is that person who is fully understanding the aggregate of form one who will fully understand the aggregate of feeling?" Answer: "No."
(b) "Or else, is that person who will fully understand the aggregate of feeling one who is fully understanding the aggregate of form?" Answer: "No."

(a) "Is that person who is not fully understanding the aggregate of form one who will not fully understand the aggregate of feeling?" Answer: "Those persons who will attain the path are not fully understanding the aggregate of form, but it is not that they will not fully understand the aggregate of feeling. The Arahats and those worldlings (puthujjanas) who will not attain the path are both not fully understanding the aggregate of form and will not fully understand the aggregate of feeling."
(b) "Or else, is that person who will not fully understand the aggregate of feeling one who is not fully understanding the aggregate of form?" Answer: "The one possessed of the path of Arahatship will not fully understand the aggregate of feeling, but it is not that he is not fully understanding the aggregate of form. The Arahats and those worldlings who will not attain the path will both not fully understand the aggregate of feeling and are not fully understanding the aggregate of form."
70:
## 6. Past-Future Portion
(a) He who has fully understood the aggregate of matter, will he fully understand the aggregate of feeling? No.
(b) Or else, he who will fully understand the aggregate of feeling, has he fully understood the aggregate of matter? No.
(a) He who has not yet fully understood the aggregate of matter, will he not fully understand the aggregate of feeling? Those who will attain the Path have not yet fully understood the aggregate of matter, but it is not that they will not fully understand the aggregate of feeling (they will). One possessed of the Path of Arahatship and those worldlings who will not attain the Path, they have not yet fully understood the aggregate of matter and they will not fully understand the aggregate of feeling.
(b) Or else, he who will not fully understand the aggregate of feeling, has he not yet fully understood the aggregate of matter? The Arahant will not fully understand the aggregate of feeling (as it is already done), but it is not that he has not fully understood the aggregate of matter (he has). One possessed of the Path of Arahatship and those worldlings who will not attain the Path, they will not fully understand the aggregate of feeling and they have not yet fully understood the aggregate of matter.

## The Section on Full Understanding is finished.

(a) Is eye the eye-base?
The divine eye (dibba-cakkhu) and the wisdom eye (paññā-cakkhu) are called 'eye', but they are not the eye-base. The eye-base is both 'eye' and 'eye-base'.
(b) Is the eye-base the eye? Yes, it is.

(a) Is ear the ear-base?
The divine ear (dibba-sota) and the ear of craving (taṇhā-sota) are called 'ear', but they are not the ear-base. The ear-base is both 'ear' and 'ear-base'.
(b) Is the ear-base the ear? Yes, it is.

For those passing away from the four-constituent and five-constituent realms, at the moment of dissolution (bhaṅgakkhaṇa) of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of arising of the Path and Fruition in the formless realm (arūpa), the Truth of Origin will cease for those persons in those places, but the Truth of Suffering does not arise. For those who have been reborn in the four-constituent and five-constituent realms, and at the moment of arising of consciousness during the course of existence, the Truth of Origin will cease and the Truth of Suffering arises for those persons in those places.

(a) For a person in a place where the Truth of Suffering arises, will the Truth of the Path (maggasacca) cease for that person in that place?

At the moment of arising of the consciousness of Arahants, for those born in the states of deprivation (apāya), for those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not obtain the Path, at the time of their rebirth, at the moment of arising of consciousness during the course of existence, and for those who have been reborn in the realm of non-percipient beings, the Truth of Suffering arises for those persons in those places, but the Truth of the Path will not cease. At the moment of arising of the Path of Arahantship, at the moment of arising of the consciousness immediately preceding the Path of Arahantship, for others who will obtain the Path at the time of their rebirth, and at the moment of arising of consciousness during the course of existence, the Truth of Suffering arises and the Truth of the Path will cease for those persons in those places.

(b) Or else, for a person in a place where the Truth of the Path will cease, does the Truth of Suffering arise for that person in that place?

At the moment of dissolution of the consciousness immediately preceding the Path of Arahantship, for others who will obtain the Path at the time of their passing away, at the moment of dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of arising of the Path and Fruition in the formless realm, the Truth of the Path will cease for those persons in those places, but the Truth of Suffering does not arise. At the moment of arising of the Path of Arahantship, at the moment of arising of the consciousness immediately preceding the Path of Arahantship, for others who will obtain the Path at the time of their rebirth, and at the moment of arising of consciousness during the course of existence, the Truth of the Path will cease and the Truth of Suffering arises for those persons in those places.

(a) For a person in a place where the Truth of Origin arises, will the Truth of the Path cease for that person in that place?

For those born in the states of deprivation, for those worldlings who will not obtain the Path, at the moment of arising of their craving (taṇhā), the Truth of Origin arises for those persons in those places, but not...
260:
...for those persons in those places, the Truth of the Path will also cease. For those who will obtain the Path, at the moment of arising of their craving, the Truth of Origin arises and the Truth of the Path will cease for those persons in those places.

(b) Or else, for a person in a place where the Truth of the Path will cease, does the Truth of Origin arise for that person in that place?

At the moment of arising of the Path of Arahantship, at the moment of arising of the consciousness immediately preceding the Path of Arahantship, for others who will obtain the Path at the moment of dissolution of their craving, and at the time when consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, the Truth of the Path will cease for those persons in those places, but the Truth of Origin does not arise. For those who will obtain the Path, at the moment of arising of their craving, the Truth of the Path will cease and the Truth of Origin arises for those persons in those places.

## (d) Paccanīka-puggala

(a) For a person for whom the Truth of Suffering (dukkhasacca) does not arise, will the Truth of Origin (samudayasacca) not cease for that person?

For all those who are passing away, at the moment of dissolution (bhaṅgakkhaṇa) of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of arising (uppādakkhaṇa) of the Path and Fruition in the formless realm (arūpa), the Truth of Suffering does not arise, but it is not the case that the Truth of Origin will not cease (it will cease). At the moment of dissolution of the Path of Arahantship (aggamagga), at the moment of dissolution of the consciousness of Arahants, at the moment of dissolution of the consciousness immediately preceding the Path of Arahantship, and at the moment of arising of the Path of Arahantship and Fruition in the formless realm, the Truth of Suffering does not arise and the Truth of Origin will not cease.

(b) Or else, for a person for whom the Truth of Origin will not cease, does the Truth of Suffering not arise for that person?

At the moment of arising of the Path of Arahantship, at the moment of arising of the consciousness of Arahants, and at the moment of arising of the consciousness immediately preceding the Path of Arahantship, the Truth of Origin will not cease, but it is not the case that the Truth of Suffering does not arise (it arises). At the moment of dissolution of the Path of Arahantship, at the moment of dissolution of the consciousness of Arahants, at the moment of dissolution of the consciousness immediately preceding the Path of Arahantship, and at the moment of arising of the Path of Arahantship and Fruition in the formless realm, the Truth of Origin will not cease and the Truth of Suffering does not arise.

(a) For a person for whom the Truth of Suffering does not arise, will the Truth of the Path (maggasacca) not cease for that person?

At the moment of dissolution of the consciousness immediately preceding the Path of Arahantship, for others who will obtain the Path at the time of their passing away, at the moment of dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of arising of the Path and Fruition in the formless realm, the Truth of Suffering does not arise, but it is not the case that the Truth of the Path will not cease (it will cease). At the moment of dissolution of the Path of Arahantship, at the moment of dissolution of the consciousness of Arahants, for worldlings (puthujjana) who will not obtain the Path...
261:
For those who are passing away, and at the moment of dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of arising of the Arahattaphala in the Arūpa realm, for those persons the Truth of Suffering does not arise, and the Truth of the Path will not cease.

(b) Alternatively, to whom the Truth of the Path will not cease, does the Truth of Suffering not arise for that person?

At the moment of arising of the consciousness of Arahants, and for those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the Path, at the time they are being reborn, and at the moment of arising of consciousness during the course of existence, for those persons the Truth of the Path will not cease, but it is not that the Truth of Suffering does not arise (it arises). At the moment of dissolution of the Arahattamagga, and at the moment of dissolution of the consciousness of Arahants, and for those worldlings who will not attain the Path, at the time they are passing away, and at the moment of dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of arising of the Arahattaphala in the Arūpa realm, for those persons the Truth of the Path will not cease, and the Truth of Suffering also does not arise.

(a) To whom the Truth of the Origin does not arise, will the Truth of the Path not cease for that person?

At the moment of arising of the Arahattamagga, and at the moment of arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the Arahattamagga, and for others who will attain the Path, at the moment of dissolution of craving (taṇhā), and while consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, and for those attained to cessation (nirodhasamāpanna), and for Asaññasatta beings, for those persons the Truth of the Origin does not arise, but it is not that the Truth of the Path will not cease (it will cease). At the moment of dissolution of the Arahattamagga, and for Arahants, and for those worldlings who will not attain the Path, at the moment of dissolution of craving, and while consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, for those persons the Truth of the Origin does not arise, and the Truth of the Path will also not cease.

(b) Alternatively, to whom the Truth of the Path will not cease, does the Truth of the Origin not arise for that person?

For those worldlings who will not attain the Path, at the moment of arising of craving, for those persons the Truth of the Path will not cease, but it is not that the Truth of the Origin does not arise (it arises). At the moment of dissolution of the Arahattamagga, and for Arahants, and for those worldlings who will not attain the Path, at the moment of dissolution of craving, and while consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, for those persons the Truth of the Path will not cease, and the Truth of the Origin also does not arise.

## (e) Negative Location (Paccanīka-okāsa)

In whichever plane the Truth of Suffering does not arise ... etc ...

## (f) Negative Person-Location (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)

(a) To whom in whichever plane the Truth of Suffering does not arise, will the Truth of the Origin not cease for that person in that plane?

For those passing away from the Catuvokāra and Pañcavokāra planes, and at the moment of dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of arising of the Path and Fruition in the Arūpa realm, for those persons the Truth of Suffering does not arise in that plane, but it is not that the Truth of the Origin will not cease for them in that plane (it will cease).
262: At the dissolving moment (bhaṅgakkhaṇa) of the Path of Arahantship (arahatta-magga), and at the dissolving moment of the consciousness of Arahants, and at the dissolving moment of that consciousness immediately after which they will obtain the Path of Arahantship, and at the arising moment (uppādakkhaṇa) of the Path of Arahantship and the Fruition in the formless realm (arūpa-bhūmi), and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta) who are passing away, for those beings in that location, Dukkha-sacca is not arising, and Samudaya-sacca will not cease. (b) Or else, for whom in which location Samudaya-sacca will not cease, for that person in that location does Dukkha-sacca not arise? At the arising moment (uppādakkhaṇa) of the Path of Arahantship, and at the arising moment of the consciousness of Arahants, and at the arising moment of that consciousness immediately after which they will obtain the Path of Arahantship, and for non-percipient beings who are being reborn (upapajjantānaṃ), for those beings in that location, Samudaya-sacca will not cease, but it is not that Dukkha-sacca is not arising (it is arising). At the dissolving moment (bhaṅgakkhaṇa) of the Path of Arahantship, and at the dissolving moment of the consciousness of Arahants, and at the dissolving moment of that consciousness immediately after which they will obtain the Path of Arahantship, and at the arising moment (uppādakkhaṇa) of the Path of Arahantship and the Fruition in the formless realm, and for non-percipient beings who are passing away, for those beings in that location, Samudaya-sacca will not cease, and Dukkha-sacca is not arising. (a) For whom in which location Dukkha-sacca is not arising, for that person in that location will Magga-sacca not cease? At the dissolving moment (bhaṅgakkhaṇa) of that consciousness immediately after which they will obtain the Path of Arahantship, and for others who will obtain the Path at the moment of passing away, and at the dissolving moment of consciousness during the course of existence (pavatti), and at the arising moment (uppādakkhaṇa) of the Path and the Fruition in the formless realm, for those beings in that location, Dukkha-sacca is not arising, but it is not that Magga-sacca will not cease (it will cease). At the dissolving moment (bhaṅgakkhaṇa) of the Path of Arahantship, and at the dissolving moment of the consciousness of Arahants, and for those in the woeful planes (apāya) and worldlings (puthujjana) who will not obtain the Path at the moment of passing away, and at the dissolving moment of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the arising moment (uppādakkhaṇa) of the Fruition of Arahantship in the formless realm, and for non-percipient beings who are passing away, for those beings in that location, Dukkha-sacca is not arising, and Magga-sacca will not cease. (b) Or else, for whom in which location Magga-sacca will not cease, for that person in that location does Dukkha-sacca not arise? At the arising moment (uppādakkhaṇa) of the consciousness of Arahants, and for those in the woeful planes and worldlings who will not obtain the Path at the moment of rebirth-linking (upapajjantānaṃ), and at the arising moment of consciousness during the course of existence, and for non-percipient beings who are being reborn, for those beings in that location, Magga-sacca will not cease, but it is not that Dukkha-sacca is not arising (it is arising). At the dissolving moment (bhaṅgakkhaṇa) of the Path of Arahantship, and at the dissolving moment of the consciousness of Arahants, and for those in the woeful planes and worldlings who will not obtain the Path at the moment of passing away, and at the dissolving moment of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the arising moment (uppādakkhaṇa) of the Fruition of Arahantship in the formless realm, and for non-percipient beings who are passing away, for those beings in that location, Magga-sacca will not cease, and Dukkha-sacca is not arising.
263:
(a) For whom in which place the Truth of the Origin does not arise, for that person in that place will the Truth of the Path not cease?
At the moment of arising of the Path of Arahantship, and for those who will attain the Path of Arahantship immediately after that mind, and for others who will attain the Path, at the moment of dissolution of their craving, and when the mind dissociated from craving is occurring, for them in that place the Truth of the Origin does not arise, but it is not that for them in that place the Truth of the Path will not cease. At the moment of dissolution of the Path of Arahantship, for Arahants, for those born in the states of deprivation, and for those worldlings who will not attain the Path, at the moment of dissolution of their craving, and when the mind dissociated from craving is occurring, and for non-percipient beings, for them in that place the Truth of the Origin does not arise and the Truth of the Path will not cease.
(b) Or else, for whom in which place the Truth of the Path will not cease, for that person in that place does the Truth of the Origin not arise?
For those born in the states of deprivation, and for those worldlings who will not attain the Path, at the moment of arising of their craving, for them in that place the Truth of the Path will not cease, but it is not that for them in that place the Truth of the Origin does not arise. At the moment of dissolution of the Path of Arahantship, for Arahants, for those born in the states of deprivation, and for those worldlings who will not attain the Path, at the moment of dissolution of their craving, and when the mind dissociated from craving is occurring, and for non-percipient beings, for them in that place the Truth of the Path will not cease and the Truth of the Origin does not arise.

## 3. Pariññāvāra
## 1. Paccuppannavāra
(a) Does he who fully understands the Truth of Suffering abandon the Truth of the Origin? Yes.
(b) Or else, does he who abandons the Truth of the Origin fully understand the Truth of Suffering? Yes.
264:
(a) Does he who does not fully understand the Truth of Suffering not abandon the Truth of the Origin? Yes.
(b) Or else... pe... Yes.
## 2. Atītavāra
(a) Did he who fully understood the Truth of Suffering abandon the Truth of the Origin? Yes.
(b) Or else... pe... Yes.
(a) Did he who did not fully understand the Truth of Suffering not abandon the Truth of the Origin? Yes.
(b) Or else... pe... Yes.
## 3. Anāgatavāra
(a) Will he who will fully understand the Truth of Suffering abandon the Truth of the Origin? Yes.
(b) Or else... pe... Yes.
(a) Will he who will not fully understand the Truth of Suffering not abandon the Truth of the Origin? Yes.
(b) Or else... pe... Yes.
## 4. Paccuppannātītavāra
(a) Does he who fully understands the Truth of Suffering abandon the Truth of the Origin? No.
(b) Or else, did he who abandoned the Truth of the Origin fully understand the Truth of Suffering? No.
(a) Does he who does not fully understand the Truth of Suffering not abandon the Truth of the Origin?
The Arahant does not fully understand the Truth of Suffering (as he has already understood it), but it is not that he did not abandon the Truth of the Origin (as he has already abandoned it). Except for the person possessed of the Path of Arahantship and the Arahant, the remaining persons do not fully understand the Truth of Suffering and did not abandon the Truth of the Origin.
(b) Or else, does he who did not abandon the Truth of the Origin not fully understand the Truth of Suffering?
The person possessed of the Path of Arahantship did not abandon the Truth of the Origin, but it is not that he does not fully understand the Truth of Suffering (as he is currently understanding it). Except for the person possessed of the Path of Arahantship and the Arahant, the remaining persons did not abandon the Truth of the Origin and do not fully understand the Truth of Suffering.
## 5. Paccuppannānāgatavāra
(a) Does he who fully understands the Truth of Suffering abandon the Truth of the Origin? No.
(b) Or else, will he who will abandon the Truth of the Origin fully understand the Truth of Suffering? No.
265:
(a) Does he who does not fully understand the Truth of Suffering not abandon the Truth of the Origin?
Those who will attain the Path do not fully understand the Truth of Suffering, but it is not that they will not abandon the Truth of the Origin (as they will abandon it). The Arahant and those worldlings who will not attain the Path do not fully understand the Truth of Suffering and will not abandon the Truth of the Origin.
(b) Or else, will he who will not abandon the Truth of the Origin not fully understand the Truth of Suffering?
The person possessed of the Path of Arahantship will not abandon the Truth of the Origin, but it is not that he does not fully understand the Truth of Suffering (as he is currently understanding it). The Arahant and those worldlings who will not attain the Path will not abandon the Truth of the Origin and do not fully understand the Truth of Suffering.
## 6. Atītānāgatavāra
(a) Did he who fully understood the Truth of Suffering abandon the Truth of the Origin? No.
(b) Or else, will he who will abandon the Truth of the Origin fully understand the Truth of Suffering? No.
(a) Did he who did not fully understand the Truth of Suffering not abandon the Truth of the Origin?
Those who will attain the Path did not fully understand the Truth of Suffering, but it is not that they will not abandon the Truth of the Origin (as they will abandon it). The person possessed of the Path of Arahantship and those worldlings who will not attain the Path did not fully understand the Truth of Suffering and will not abandon the Truth of the Origin.
(b) Or else, will he who will not abandon the Truth of the Origin not fully understand the Truth of Suffering?
The Arahant will not abandon the Truth of the Origin, but it is not that he did not fully understand the Truth of Suffering (as he has already understood it). The person possessed of the Path of Arahantship and those worldlings who will not attain the Path will not abandon the Truth of the Origin and did not fully understand the Truth of Suffering.
